title: Disaster Recovery, RTO/RPO, and Business Continuity
bodyMarkdown:
## Why this matters for the PCA exam

Disaster recovery (DR) and business continuity questions are frequent. You must translate **business requirements** (how much downtime and data loss is tolerable) into the **right architecture** at the right cost. The two anchor metrics are RTO and RPO.

## RTO vs RPO

- **RPO (Recovery Point Objective)** = maximum acceptable **data loss**, measured in time. It drives **backup/replication frequency**. RPO of 5 minutes means you must capture data at least every 5 minutes (often continuous replication).
- **RTO (Recovery Time Objective)** = maximum acceptable **downtime**, measured in time. It drives the **recovery architecture** (how fast you can be serving again).

> Tip: RPO looks **backward** (how much data since the last good copy). RTO looks **forward** (how long until we are back up).

## The DR pattern spectrum

Cost rises as RTO/RPO shrink:

| Pattern | RTO | RPO | Ongoing cost | Description |
|---------|-----|-----|--------------|-------------|
| **Backup & restore (cold)** | Hours+ | Hours (backup interval) | Lowest | Rebuild infra and restore data after a disaster |
| **Pilot light** | Tens of minutes | Minutes | Low-medium | Core data replicated; minimal infra kept ready to scale |
| **Warm standby** | Minutes | Seconds-minutes | Medium-high | Scaled-down running copy; scale up on failover |
| **Hot standby / active-active** | Near zero | Near zero | Highest | Full duplicate(s) serving live; traffic reroutes automatically |

## Mapping patterns to Google Cloud services

- **Backups:** Cloud Storage (with object versioning, retention, dual-region/multi-region), Persistent Disk snapshots, Cloud SQL automated backups + **point-in-time recovery (PITR)**, Backup and DR Service.
- **Replication / HA:** Cloud SQL **HA** (synchronous regional standby), cross-region **read replicas**, Spanner multi-region (synchronous, strong consistency), Bigtable replication.
- **Traffic management & failover:** **global external Application Load Balancer**, Cloud DNS routing policies, multi-region MIGs.
- **Automation:** infrastructure-as-code (Terraform) so a cold/warm environment can be rebuilt or scaled deterministically; runbooks tested regularly.

## Choosing the right tier

1. Ask the business for the **RTO and RPO** of each critical service - not all services need the same tier.
2. Pick the **cheapest pattern that meets** the objectives. Do not over-engineer non-critical systems with active-active.
3. For region-loss survival with near-zero RPO/RTO, you need **multi-region active-active** with near-synchronous replication.
4. **Test the plan**: a DR plan that is never exercised is a guess. Run regular failover drills and validate the actual recovery time.

## Business continuity beyond infrastructure

Business continuity is broader than DR: it includes people, processes, communication plans, and dependencies. A complete plan covers who declares an incident, how stakeholders are notified, and how the business operates in degraded mode while recovery proceeds.

## Key takeaways

- **RPO = data loss; RTO = downtime.** Smaller objectives cost more.
- Match the **DR pattern** (cold/pilot-light/warm/hot) to the business objective and budget.
- Region-loss with near-zero loss => **multi-region active-active**.
- Always **test** the DR plan; automate recovery with IaC.
